title: RamanujanNestedRadicals: convergence and exact values of Ramanujan-type nested radicals
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the results of the author's paper "Nested Radicals of Ramanujan's Type with Arbitrary Coefficient Sequences" (Flamandzki, 2026). For a coefficient sequence a : N -> R, the radical of depth d is built by the recursion R_k = sqrt(1 + a_k R_{k+1}) from a seed; `Submission.rollUp a T d` is the depth-d truncation with seed T and `Submission.truncRadical a d` uses the seed 1. For a root order n >= 2 the square root is replaced by the n-th root (`Submission.rollUpN`) and, for the classical unbounded family, by the signed recursion with radicand (-1)^n + a_k R_{k+1} (`Submission.rollUpNS`), whose coefficients are a_k = altSum n (N + k - 1) for the alternating polynomial altSum n x = x^(n-1) - x^(n-2) + ... +- 1. Four statements are submitted: (1) for real N >= 2 and a_k = N + k - 2 the square-root truncations converge to exactly N (for N = 3 this is Ramanujan's radical; the statement is known, see the sources, and is the base case); (2) for every root order n >= 2, both parities, the truncations of the signed family converge to exactly N, which is not treated in the sources listed below (the only place where parity enters is the sign (-1)^n); (3) an arbitrary-profile theorem: if R_k >= 1 and the coefficients are the ones for which R satisfies the recursion exactly, R_k^n = 1 + a_k R_{k+1}, then the depth-d truncation with seed 1 satisfies 0 <= R_1 - T_d <= R_1 prod_{j<d} (1 - 1/R_j), and it converges to exactly R_1 whenever the sum of 1/R_k diverges (it contains every constant profile and the classical family for every even n, with an explicit rate; it is not stated in version 2 of the paper; version 3 states it). The development (`RamanujanNested/`, 24 modules) contains further results that are not advertised in `Challenge.lean`: boundedness and monotonicity, controlled negative coefficients, the inverse construction, the closed-form identity chain for every n, the constant-coefficient exact-target radical for every n, an oscillatory family, and existence of a limit for linear and prime coefficient families at every root order. The paper's numerical tables, algorithms as running code, and informal discussion are not formalized. Zero sorries; depends only on the three standard Lean axioms.
